title: I WOULD go ALL IN this 1 Stock‼️

steps.does: Shows a screenshot of the brokerage account overview in an image viewer: account value, daily dollar and percent change, and the 3-year chart and rate of return.
steps.why: To show the account is at an all-time high and that the portfolio is compounding.
data: 3Y equity curve from Sep 2023 to Sep 2026
steps.conclusion: Account at a new all-time high.

steps.does: Calls out the day's dollar move and the total gain of individual holdings, then shows a table of six holdings with daily and total gain/loss columns (also posted on X).
steps.why: To show which positions are moving the account and how large each is.
steps.conclusion: Gains are broad across several individual stocks, not just the index.

rules.text: Be an individual stock picker rather than relying on the market going up: choose the best companies, which let the account hit highs even when the Nasdaq is range-bound.

steps.does: Asked to pick one of six holdings for 6 years, ranks them: AMD is the pick for 6 months, Celsius has the most 6-year upside (Celsius and Alani brands, more SKUs, doors, international, margin and EPS).
steps.why: To separate pure upside from the overall best risk-reward.
data: Expansion: US, international, more SKUs, more doors
steps.conclusion: Celsius has the most upside but not the pick.

steps.does: Rejects Celsius because of single-category risk (a move away from caffeine or energy drinks, brand damage); picks Elf for multiple strong brands (Elf, Naturium, Rhode), acquisition record, shelf-space and SKU headroom, international and margin/EPS growth and a clean financial setup. Cheesecake Factory has pulled forward gains at $100+; Estee Lauder is a dividend value stock; AMD faces a possible semiconductor slowdown around 2028.
steps.why: To find the most attractive risk-reward over 6 years.
steps.conclusion: Elf is the all-in pick for 6 years.

steps.does: Explains the pick is the smallest position in the public account because he already holds heavily in private portfolios (about $300-400k in one).
steps.why: Position sizing is judged on total exposure, not one account.
data: Elf is a smallest-value position in the shown account
About $300-400k Elf in one private portfolio
Held in almost every private portfolio
steps.conclusion: Comfortable with current Elf sizing in the public account.

rules.text: Always account for how much of a stock is held across all portfolios when sizing a position.
Be wary of the largest-upside name if it carries a single-category risk; prefer multiple strong brands for the long horizon.

steps.does: Plays CNBC segments on YouTube (Tom Lee on a 'face ripper' rally; Nasdaq surge debate) showing index and 10-year yield readings on the CNBC ticker, then reacts to claims about the S&P 500, sentiment and individual stocks.
steps.why: To react to Wall Street views and contrast them with his own approach.
data: 100-day moving average cited as the pullback low
steps.conclusion: Contrarian: bearish sentiment is a mistake; stay invested and be selective with individual stocks.

rules.text: He will feel more bearish when everybody feels more bullish; a bearish sentiment backdrop is not a reason to de-risk.
